paras.en: “Just finding a dwarf planet so quickly, maybe we’ll find something even bigger,” she says. “There could be something the size of Mars out there. And then we’d have the whole planet debate all over again. It would be fun.”
paras.zh: “这么快就找到了一颗矮行星，也许我们会发现更大的东西，”她说。 “那里可能有火星大小的东西。然后我们会再次进行整个星球的辩论。这会很有趣。”

articles.title: A drug-free diabetes treatment? An implant lowers blood sugar in mice
articles.author: Isha Ishtiaq

paras.en: A wireless implant that clears excess sugar from the blood could someday offer a drug-free way to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity.
paras.zh: 一种清除血液中多余糖分的无线植入物有一天可能会提供一种无需药物的方法来治疗 2 型糖尿病和肥胖症。

paras.en: In mice with both conditions, the under-the-skin device brought high blood sugar back to normal within 60 to 90 minutes of being switched on, researchers report October 22 in Science. After six weeks, the treated mice lost up to 10 percent of their body weight and had lower triglycerides, a type of fat in the blood.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 10 月 22 日在《科学》杂志上报道，在患有这两种情况的小鼠中，皮下装置在启动后 60 至 90 分钟内使高血糖恢复正常。六周后，接受治疗的小鼠体重减轻了 10%，甘油三酯（血液中的一种脂肪）也降低了。

paras.en: Diabetes affects about 830 million people worldwide. Conventional type 2 diabetes treatments like insulin and GLP-1 drugs require careful dosing. Even experimental diabetes-controlling implants still rely on the hormone insulin, which clears sugar from the bloodstream but doesn’t rid the body of it, says Martin Fussenegger, a bioengineer at ETH Zurich. The new implant instead removes glucose from the body without added drugs, genes or living cells.
paras.zh: 糖尿病影响全球约 8.3 亿人。胰岛素和 GLP-1 药物等传统 2 型糖尿病治疗需要谨慎给药。苏黎世联邦理工学院的生物工程师马丁·富森格 (Martin Fussenegger) 表示，即使是实验性的糖尿病控制植入物仍然依赖于胰岛素激素，胰岛素可以清除血液中的糖分，但不会消除体内的糖分。新的植入物可以从体内去除葡萄糖，无需添加药物、基因或活细胞。

paras.en: The 3-centimeter-long device contains a catalyst made of gold flakes and platinum particles on spongelike graphite. When electricity powers it, the catalyst converts glucose into gluconate, a compound that is easier for the kidneys to flush out in urine. With less glucose available for energy, the body may turn to its fat stores instead, Fussenegger and colleagues suspect. In mice, that shift showed up as higher blood levels of chemicals released when fat breaks down, such as ketones. “This system kind of targets the root cause, which is the energy surplus by glucose in the body,” Fussenegger says.
paras.zh: 这个3厘米长的装置包含由金片和铂颗粒在海绵状石墨上制成的催化剂。当电力为其提供动力时，催化剂将葡萄糖转化为葡萄糖酸盐，这种化合物更容易被肾脏从尿液中排出。富塞内格和同事怀疑，由于可用于提供能量的葡萄糖减少，身体可能会转而使用脂肪储存。在小鼠中，这种转变表现为脂肪分解时血液中释放的化学物质（例如酮）水平升高。 “这个系统的目标是根本原因，即体内葡萄糖的能量过剩，”富塞内格说。

paras.en: The implant works like an automatic sugar-removal system: A wearable glucose monitor detects high blood sugar levels and sends readings through a smartphone that switches the implant on. When levels return to a safer range, it switches off. The automated system ran for two weeks in eight mice. The catalyst itself remained able to convert glucose after up to three months under their skin, though the study didn’t establish how long the entire device would last.
paras.zh: 该植入物的工作原理类似于自动除糖系统：可穿戴式血糖监测仪可检测高血糖水平，并通过打开植入物的智能手机发送读数。当水平恢复到更安全的范围时，它就会关闭。该自动化系统在八只小鼠身上运行​​了两周。尽管该研究没有确定整个装置能持续多久，但催化剂本身在皮肤下放置三个月后仍然能够转化葡萄糖。

paras.en: And it’s still unknown how well the device would work in people. “This is a potentially promising method,” says David Klonoff, an endocrinologist at Sutter Mills-Peninsula Medical Center in Burlingame, Calif., who was not involved in the study. “But the risks are significant and must be carefully ruled out before it can be safely tested on humans.”
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚该设备在人体中的效果如何。 “这是一种潜在有前途的方法，”加利福尼亚州伯林格姆萨特米尔斯半岛医疗中心的内分泌学家戴维·克洛诺夫（David Klonoff）说，他没有参与这项研究。 “但风险很大，必须仔细排除，然后才能在人体上进行安全测试。”

paras.en: Researchers need to determine how much gluconate the kidneys can clear, Klonoff says. If it builds up, it could disrupt the body’s acid-base balance, causing symptoms such as nausea or confusion; excreting it could also deplete electrolytes such as sodium and potassium, he notes.
paras.zh: 克洛诺夫说，研究人员需要确定肾脏可以清除多少葡萄糖酸。如果它积聚起来，可能会破坏身体的酸碱平衡，导致恶心或神智不清等症状；他指出，排出体外还会消耗钠和钾等电解质。

paras.en: Scaling up the device is another challenge. Humans consume about 250 grams of carbohydrates daily, compared with two grams for mice, Klonoff estimates. Meeting that demand could require a much larger implant or multiple devices, he says. In a lab test, a larger device cleared nearly all glucose from about 5 liters of solution, roughly an adult’s blood volume, though not a full day’s glucose intake.
paras.zh: 扩大设备规模是另一个挑战。 Klonoff 估计，人类每天消耗约 250 克碳水化合物，而小鼠则为 2 克。他说，满足这一需求可能需要更大的植入物或多个设备。在一项实验室测试中，一台更大的设备几乎清除了大约 5 升溶液中的所有葡萄糖，这大约是一个成年人的血容量，但还不是一整天的葡萄糖摄入量。

paras.en: Fussenegger’s team plans to test the device in pigs and sheep before considering human trials. If proven safe and effective, it could offer an alternative to existing diabetes treatments and a new weight-loss option for people regardless of whether they have diabetes, he says.
paras.zh: 富塞内格的团队计划在考虑人体试验之前先在猪和羊身上测试该装置。他说，如果被证明安全有效，它可以为现有糖尿病治疗提供一种替代方案，并为人们提供新的减肥选择，无论他们是否患有糖尿病。

articles.title: Your voice can now say things you never said
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: AI technology can create realistic clones of people’s voices. The resulting proliferation of synthetic voices ushers in all sorts of new scenarios, good and bad. “Today, with nothing more than a keyboard and an internet connection, you can type, and you can get an image, a voice, a video of anything, [of] anybody doing or saying anything,” says Hany Farid, a computer scientist at Dartmouth University.
paras.zh: 人工智能技术可以创建真实的人声克隆。由此产生的合成声音的激增带来了各种新的场景，无论好坏。达特茅斯大学计算机科学家哈尼·法里德 (Hany Farid) 表示：“如今，只需键盘和互联网连接，你就可以打字，并且可以获得任何内容的图像、声音、视频，以及任何人所做或所说的任何事情。”

paras.en: Some of these voice clones are deeply meaningful to people, as in the cases of people who lost their ability to speak. But voice clones can also cause harm, as with scams and deepfakes. And some uses fall into murky gray zones, such as voice clones that “speak” after a person has passed away. What happens to a person’s digital voice after they’re gone?
paras.zh: 其中一些声音克隆对人们具有深远的意义，就像那些失去说话能力的人一样。但声音克隆也可能造成伤害，例如诈骗和深度伪造。有些用途属于灰色地带，例如在人去世后“说话”的声音克隆。一个人去世后，他的数字声音会怎样？

paras.en: In this episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me, hear more from Farid, as well as from a former hospital chaplain and AI researcher, and from Jules Rodriguez, a man who communicates with a voice clone. You’ll also hear about a choice Jules made about what will happen to his voice once he’s gone.
paras.zh: 在《深渊：与我交谈》的这一集中，您将听到法里德、前医院牧师和人工智能研究员以及通过声音克隆进行交流的朱尔斯·罗德里格斯的更多信息。您还会听到朱尔斯做出的选择，即他去世后他的声音会发生什么变化。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: What’s a voice you like to listen to?
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：你喜欢听什么声音？

paras.en: Kate Nilson: That is a great question. I hope my students don’t listen to this. I was having Snoop Dogg read their assignments to me the other day, just because I thought it was funny. But I don’t know if I would say that’s my favorite.
paras.zh: 凯特·尼尔森：这是一个很好的问题。我希望我的学生不要听这个。有一天，我让史努比狗狗给我读他们的作业，只是因为我觉得这很有趣。但我不知道我是否会说这是我的最爱。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech language pathologist and professor Kate Nilson. And if you’re wondering, this is a real, legitimate thing that anyone can do.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是言语病理学家兼教授凯特·尼尔森。如果你想知道，这是任何人都可以做的真实、合法的事情。

paras.en: Snoop Dogg audio: Vector mathematics. Think about a car trip. Your displacement from your starting point is a vector.
paras.zh: Snoop Dogg 音频：矢量数学。想想开车旅行。从起点开始的位移是一个向量。

paras.en: Snoop Dogg: I’m glad to be the voice of reason so you can focus better, understand more, and enjoy listening to the internet in the voice of Snoop Dogg.
paras.zh: Snoop Dogg：我很高兴成为理性的声音，这样您就可以更好地集中注意力，了解更多，并享受以 Snoop Dogg 的声音收听互联网。

paras.en: Sanders: Welcome to The Deep End, Talk To Me. In this episode, we’re stepping out of the lab and into the new digital world we all live in. We’re going to get into some of the good, bad and strange scenarios that come up when voices can be cloned and let loose in the world. Let’s talk about it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：欢迎来到深渊，跟我谈谈。在这一集中，我们将走出实验室，进入我们都生活的新数字世界。我们将进入当声音可以被克隆并在世界上释放时出现的一些好的、坏的和奇怪的场景。我们来谈谈吧。

paras.en: [voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? Hi. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi. Your voice is you.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？你好。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。你的声音就是你。

paras.en: Sanders: As we’ve heard in earlier episodes, ultra-realistic voice clones can be extremely meaningful to people who can no longer speak.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：正如我们在前几集中听到的那样，超现实的声音克隆对于无法说话的人来说非常有意义。

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: So when I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared. When my wife first heard it, she cried because of how close it sounded like me before I lost my voice. I knew of the potential of this technology at that moment.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：所以当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。当我妻子第一次听到这首歌时，她哭了，因为这听起来太像我失声之前的我了。那一刻我就知道了这项技术的潜力。

paras.en: Sanders: These digital copies of voices have restored connections to their loved ones.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些声音的数字副本已经恢复了他们与亲人的联系。

paras.en: MA Fernandez: You know, the first thing he played for me, I was like chills all over.
paras.zh: MA Fernandez：你知道，他为我演奏的第一首曲子，我浑身发冷。

paras.en: Patrick Darling: The first time I performed with the AI voice, I was surprised how physically connected I felt with it.
paras.zh: 帕特里克·达林：我第一次用人工智能声音表演时，我很惊讶我与它的身体联系。

paras.en: Sanders: These voice clones have been transformative for people who have lost the ability to talk. But the existence of realistic digital copies of voices has effects that ripple farther out into society.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些声音克隆对于那些失去说话能力的人来说是变革性的。但真实的声音数字副本的存在会对社会产生更深远的影响。

paras.en: Hany Farid: So here’s where sort of state of the art is. Today, with nothing more than a keyboard and an internet connection, you can type and you can get an image, a voice, a video of anything, anybody doing or saying anything.
paras.zh: Hany Farid：这就是最先进的地方。如今，只需键盘和互联网连接，您就可以打字，并且可以获得任何内容、任何人所做或所说的任何图像、声音、视频。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Hany Farid. He’s a computer scientist at Dartmouth College and cofounder of Get Real Security, a firm that sorts real from fake. I called him to ask how these voice clones have changed our world.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是汉尼·法里德。他是达特茅斯学院的计算机科学家，也是 Get Real Security 的联合创始人，这是一家辨别真假的公司。我打电话给他，询问这些声音克隆如何改变了我们的世界。

paras.en: Farid: If you had asked me, I don’t know, five years ago, is this possible? I would say, yeah, maybe, but not anytime soon. And then all of a sudden, boom, it just came out of nowhere.
paras.zh: Farid：如果你五年前问我，我不知道这可能吗？我会说，是的，也许吧，但不会很快。然后突然之间，砰的一声，它就凭空出现了。

paras.en: Sanders: This shift happened in a very, very short amount of time, and it has big implications, both good and bad.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这种转变发生在非常非常短的时间内，它产生了巨大的影响，无论好坏。

paras.en: Farid: And so we are living in, I think, in equal parts an exciting time and a terrifying time, and somehow those are coexisting.
paras.zh: 法里德：我认为，我们生活在一个激动人心的时代和一个可怕的时代，而且不知何故，这些时代是共存的。

paras.en: Sanders: Farid tells me about some of his research, which asks people to decide whether something, like a voice or a video, is real.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德向我介绍了他的一些研究，该研究要求人们判断某些事物（例如声音或视频）是否真实。

paras.en: Farid: My bread and butter is developing technologies to distinguish real from fake. And we work with media outlets and law enforcement and courts, et cetera. But one of the questions you always want to ask when you’re in my business is, well, do you need the mathematics and the computation? Just let somebody listen to it or look at it. And can they tell the difference?
paras.zh: Farid：我的面包和黄油正在开发区分真假的技术。我们与媒体、执法部门和法院等合作。但是，当你从事我的业务时，你总是想问的问题之一是，你需要数学和计算吗？只要让某人听或看即可。他们能分辨出区别吗？

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out they cannot. In laboratory tests, people can’t reliably say whether a voice they hear was created by a machine or by a real living, breathing person.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明他们不能。在实验室测试中，人们无法可靠地判断他们听到的声音是由机器发出的还是由真实存在的、会呼吸的人发出的。

paras.en: Farid: It’s essentially like they’re flipping a coin.
paras.zh: Farid：这本质上就像他们在掷硬币。

paras.en: Sanders: But there’s another, even higher bar for voice clones to pass. That’s whether they can mimic a specific person well enough to slip by undetected.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是声音克隆还有另一个甚至更高的门槛。问题在于它们是否能够很好地模仿特定的人，从而在不被发现的情况下溜走。

paras.en: Farid: The other question too is what if I, for example, play a real voice sample of your voice, Laura, and then I clone your voice using my favorite AI cloning technology, and then I type something and I get you to say something, and I play those two samples to somebody, and I don’t ask them if it’s real/fake. I say, is this the same person? Is the AI not only able to make something that is natural, but is it identity preserving?
paras.zh: Farid：另一个问题是，如果我播放你声音的真实声音样本，劳拉，然后我使用我最喜欢的人工智能克隆技术克隆你的声音，然后我输入一些东西，让你说一些东西，然后我向某人播放这两个样本，我不会问他们是真是假。我说，这是同一个人吗？人工智能不仅能够制造出自然的东西，而且还能保留身份吗？

paras.en: Sanders: Okay, give it a try yourself. Is this the same person?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：好吧，你自己尝试一下。这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] And how about now? Is this the same person?
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]现在怎么样？这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: Farid: And when you ask them, is it the same person? They say yes, which means the AI has figured out with roughly 20 seconds or so of your voice how to make their AI sound like you, which is mind-blowing.
paras.zh: Farid：当你问他们时，是同一个人吗？他们说是，这意味着人工智能已经通过你大约 20 秒左右的声音弄清楚了如何让他们的人工智能听起来像你，这令人兴奋。

paras.en: Sanders: In the earlier episodes of this season, you’ve heard examples of the good that’s been created by these technological leaps. In many cases, that good comes because these voices are both extremely realistic and extremely good at sounding like a specific person. People want their voice to sound like theirs.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在本季的前几集中，你已经听说过这些技术飞跃所创造的美好例子。在许多情况下，这种好处的出现是因为这些声音非常真实，而且非常擅长听起来像特定的人。人们希望自己的声音听起来像自己的。

paras.en: Farid: People with ALS can speak with what sounds like their voice. We’ve seen beautiful examples of that. Translation, right? We can now translate things in real time from any language and it’ll sound like you. I’ve made videos of myself speaking any language I want and it sounds like me, and it’s amazing. It’s really cool.
paras.zh: Farid：患有 ALS 的人可以用听起来像他们自己的声音说话。我们已经看到了这方面的美丽例子。翻译一下吧？我们现在可以实时翻译任何语言的内容，而且听起来就像您一样。我制作了自己说任何我想要的语言的视频，听起来就像我一样，这太棒了。真的很酷。

paras.en: Sanders: These new ways to connect are very impressive, but as with any technology, these powerful realistic auditory dupes can be repurposed to cause harm.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些新的连接方式令人印象深刻，但与任何技术一样，这些强大的现实听觉欺骗可以被重新利用以造成伤害。

paras.en: Farid: Some pretty bad stuff’s happening, right? So let’s just go through a few of these. So first, you’re seeing massive types of fraud. Everything from romance scams to people calling parents and saying your kids have been taken, pay a ransom, to geopolitics. People are getting on calls with who they think are leaders of other countries, and it’s not. It’s a deepfake. It’s an AI-generated voice or face.
paras.zh: Farid：一些非常糟糕的事情正在发生，对吧？让我们来看看其中的一些。首先，您会看到大量类型的欺诈行为。从爱情骗局到人们打电话给父母并说你的孩子被带走了，要支付赎金，再到地缘政治。人们正在与他们认为是其他国家领导人的人通话，但事实并非如此。这是一个深度伪造。这是人工智能生成的声音或面孔。

paras.en: Sanders: What Farid is saying feels especially relevant right now. I’m recording this episode in the fall of 2026, and midterm elections in the U.S. are upon us. Political ads are everywhere. Some of these ads use deepfake audio and video to make opponents say or do things they never did. Here are a few recent examples of deepfakes compiled by the New York Times.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德所说的话现在感觉特别有意义。我在 2026 年秋天录制这一集，美国中期选举即将到来。政治广告无处不在。其中一些广告使用深度伪造的音频和视频来让对手说或做他们从未做过的事情。以下是《纽约时报》最近整理的一些深度伪造的例子。

paras.en: [Audio] Hi, I’m Zohran Mamdani and I’m Kathy Hochul and together, we’re making New York, don’t say affordable. I’m voting for Hochul because she basically gave me an early retirement. They stopped prosecuting people for crime, so now I get to sit back and play Candy Crush all day. Is New York getting a little expensive? I’m Kathy Hochul, and I’ve got just the thing. Clinton lover, Trump hater.
paras.zh: [音频] 大家好，我是 Zohran Mamdani，我是 Kathy Hochul，我们一起打造纽约，更不用说负担得起了。我投票给 Hochul 因为她基本上让我提前退休。他们不再起诉犯罪分子，所以现在我可以坐下来玩一整天的《糖果粉碎传奇》。纽约是不是有点贵了？我是凯西·霍赫尔（Kathy Hochul），我就是这样。克林顿的爱人，特朗普的仇恨者。

paras.en: Farid: When you can steal somebody’s likeness, their voice, and their face, you can do some damage. We’re seeing people doing content credential resets at companies. They call up and say, oh, I’m employee X. Will you reset my credential? That’s how they’re now attacking companies. We’re seeing North Korean IT workers penetrating Fortune 500 companies by disguising their voices and their accents and their identities. So lots of bad things, and not unpredictably bad.
paras.zh: 法里德：当你可以窃取某人的肖像、声音和面孔时，你就可以造成一些损害。我们看到人们在公司进行内容凭证重置。他们打电话说，哦，我是员工 X。您能重置我的凭据吗？这就是他们现在攻击公司的方式。我们看到朝鲜 IT 员工通过伪装声音、口音和身份渗透到财富 500 强公司。所以有很多坏事，但并不是不可预测的坏事。

paras.en: Sanders: There are romance scams, political scams, employment scams, money scams of all sorts. Farid was even involved in one himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有爱情骗局、政治骗局、就业骗局、金钱骗局等等。法里德本人甚至也参与其中。

paras.en: Farid: My voice was cloned by an attacker. I was working a very sensitive case with an attorney. Not many people knew about it. And he got a call from my phone number in my voice talking about the case. And after about three minutes, got suspicious, hung up, called me back. Wasn’t me.
paras.zh: Farid：我的声音被攻击者克隆了。我正在和一位律师一起处理一个非常敏感的案件。没有多少人知道这件事。他接到了我的电话号码，用我的声音谈论了这个案子。大约三分钟后，我开始怀疑，挂断电话，给我回了电话。不是我。

paras.en: Sanders: With the proliferation of AI chatbots to write the scripts for these fake voices, these scams can be deployed on a very large scale. That means there’s no human in the loop except for the person getting scammed. There’s something depressing about the loss of this extremely personal information. And the worst part is that these cloned voices feel like they’re just the latest piece of privacy eroding.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：随着人工智能聊天机器人为这些虚假声音编写脚本的激增，这些骗局可以大规模部署。这意味着除了被骗的人之外，没有人参与其中。丢失这些极其个人的信息是令人沮丧的。最糟糕的是，这些克隆声音让人感觉它们只是最新的隐私侵蚀行为。

paras.en: Farid: For a long time, it was our social security numbers, our ability to access our bank accounts were held very tight. And then it’s like, all right, that’s over. Everybody’s got my social security. All the privacy problems of the last 20 years. So we’ve given up what we call PII, personally identifiable information. You can find my phone number, my address, my social security number, everything about me. And that’s true of almost every single American and every person in the world. All right, so that barrier was shattered, whatever, a few years ago. But then we held on to, okay, but I’ve got me, my voice, my likeness. Yeah, not so much. So now imagine that you have all the information you need about you, Laura, me, anybody, and now you can mimic me. Think about how powerful that is. And think about also how helpless I am. I have no control on the billions of calls unfolding every day, every hour, if somebody has co-opted my likeness.
paras.zh: 法里德：很长一段时间以来，我们的社会安全号码、我们访问银行账户的能力都受到严格控制。然后就好像，好吧，就这样结束了。每个人都有我的社会保障。过去 20 年的所有隐私问题。因此，我们放弃了所谓的 PII，即个人身份信息。你可以找到我的电话号码、我的地址、我的社会安全号码，以及关于我的一切。几乎每个美国人和世界上每个人都是如此。好吧，无论如何，几年前这个障碍就被打破了。但后来我们坚持了下来，好吧，但我有我自己，我的声音，我的肖像。是的，没那么多。现在想象一下，你拥有关于你、劳拉、我、任何人的所有信息，现在你可以模仿我。想想那有多么强大。也想想我是多么的无助。如果有人盗用了我的肖像，我无法控制每天、每小时发生的数十亿个电话。

paras.en: Sanders: Bigger picture, we’ve reached a point where it’s safe to say we can no longer automatically trust digital versions of other people. That applies to the images and sounds on my computer screen as I talked with Farid. Maybe this 2-D picture and sound coming from my laptop is a fake.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从更大的角度来看，我们已经到了可以肯定地说我们不能再自动信任其他人的数字版本的地步。这适用于我与法里德交谈时电脑屏幕上的图像和声音。也许我笔记本电脑上发出的二维图像和声音是假的。

paras.en: Farid: So this two-dimensional version that you and I are sharing now, all right, I can’t control that. That can be stolen. The three-dimensional is right now still me, right? We don’t have the robots that can mimic us. Yet is the end of that sentence.
paras.zh: Farid：所以你和我现在分享的这个二维版本，好吧，我无法控制。那可以被盗。现在的三维还是我吧？我们没有可以模仿我们的机器人。然而这句话已经结束了。

paras.en: Sanders: So my interview with Farid was alarming. There are parallels here to any new technology, though. Today, people talk about brain rot from junk online. But remember that television was also going to rot our brains.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以我对法里德的采访令人震惊。不过，这与任何新技术都有相似之处。如今，人们谈论网络垃圾导致的大脑腐烂。但请记住，电视也会腐蚀我们的大脑。

paras.en: [Audio] Its content affects us. So does the sheer weight of the hours we watch.
paras.zh: [音频]它的内容影响着我们。我们观看的时间的绝对重量也是如此。

paras.en: Sanders: Phones today are the downfall of society, but actual wired telephones encountered really similar resistance when they first started appearing in homes.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：今天的电话是社会的衰落，但真正的有线电话在刚开始出现在家庭中时也遇到了类似的阻力。

paras.en: [Audio] In Chicago, Sharon Krall’s 15-year-old daughter Angie got so addicted to one teen talk line, she ran up an $850 bill in one month.
paras.zh: [音频] 在芝加哥，莎朗·克拉尔 (Sharon Krall) 15 岁的女儿安吉 (Angie) 沉迷于青少年谈话台词，一个月内就花光了 850 美元的账单。

paras.en: Sanders: No big technological advance has escaped this fear.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：任何重大的技术进步都无法逃脱这种恐惧。

paras.en: [Audio] We need teachers who are deeply concerned about how the modern media of communication are changing education.
paras.zh: [音频]我们需要深切关注现代传播媒体如何改变教育的教师。

paras.en: Sanders: Electricity, bicycles, railways, novels, even the printing press all had their skeptics. So this fear of the new thing has been around a long time. Are synthetic voices created by AI any different? Here’s Karina Nagin from Bridging Voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：电力、自行车、铁路、小说，甚至印刷机都有怀疑论者。所以这种对新事物的恐惧已经存在很长时间了。人工智能创建的合成声音有什么不同吗？这是来自 Bridging Voice 的卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 的报道。

paras.en: Nagin: Taking off my Bridging Voice hat and just as like a human being in the world, I think there’s a lot of things about AI that I’m very concerned. Deepfakes, the ability to make videos and audio that sound and look just like someone saying something that they’re not saying, I think is a huge, huge concern to our news and public information.
paras.zh: Nagin：摘下我的桥接语音帽子，就像世界上的人类一样，我认为人工智能有很多我非常关心的事情。 Deepfakes，即制作视频和音频听起来和看起来就像有人在说他们没有说的话的能力，我认为这是我们新闻和公共信息的一个巨大的担忧。

paras.en: Sanders: Nagin then pivots back to the good, the possibilities here.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：纳金然后回到好的方面，这里的可能性。

paras.en: Nagin: And then I put on my little hat in my space that I am like, this is how we can harness this to impact people’s lives in our space right now. And I think both conversations need to happen.
paras.zh: 纳金：然后我在我的空间里戴上我的小帽子，我想，这就是我们如何利用它来影响我们空间中人们的生活。我认为这两种对话都需要进行。

paras.en: Sanders: It occurs to me that I’m seeing the ends of the spectrum here. The stories Farid told me were awful. And the stories that Jules and Casey and others have told me were really, really life-changingly good. Yet these ends of the spectrum are the easy ones. The ones you can look at and say, that’s a horrible way to use this technology. Or that is a powerful and good way to use a voice clone. Between those two poles is the middle ground. That’s the place where Snoop explains cell biology.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我觉得我看到了这个范围的两端。法里德给我讲的故事很糟糕。朱尔斯、凯西和其他人告诉我的故事真的非常非常好，足以改变我的生活。然而，这些极端都是容易的。你可以看到并说，这是使用这项技术的可怕方式。或者说，这是使用语音克隆的一种强大且良好的方法。这两极之间是中间立场。这就是 Snoop 解释细胞生物学的地方。

paras.en: [Audio] The membrane separates the material outside the cell.
paras.zh: [音频] 膜将细胞外的物质分开。

paras.en: Sanders: Good, because it’s helping people learn more about mitochondria and who couldn’t use more of that in their lives. Bad, because Snoop never actually said those words, and it’s weird to pretend otherwise.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它可以帮助人们更多地了解线粒体，以及那些在生活中无法使用更多线粒体的人。糟糕的是，因为史努比实际上从未说过这些话，而且假装不说也很奇怪。

paras.en: [Audio] The artists of the Renaissance said that man’s main concern should be for man.
paras.zh: [音频]文艺复兴时期的艺术家说，人的主要关心应该是为了人。

paras.en: Sanders: There are deepfakes of the late great physicist Richard Feynman delivering famous lectures.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：已故伟大物理学家理查德·费曼发表著名演讲的深度伪造品。

paras.en: [Audio] The problem is the laws of physics themselves. Let me start with something basic. The next star over from us is called Proxima Centauri.
paras.zh: [音频] 问题在于物理定律本身。让我从一些基本的事情开始。我们附近的下一颗恒星叫做比邻星。

paras.en: Sanders: Good because it introduces some amazing physics to people who would otherwise scroll past? Bad because it’s somewhat disrespectful and possibly inaccurate? There aren’t easy answers here. This murky middle gets even murkier with the invention of griefbots. Those are digital versions of people who have passed away. And that means that special voices can keep talking to us long after the body that created them is gone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它向那些原本会滚动过去的人介绍了一些令人惊奇的物理学？不好是因为它有点不尊重而且可能不准确？这里没有简单的答案。随着悲伤机器人的发明，这个阴暗的中间变得更加阴暗。这些是已故之人的数字版本。这意味着特殊的声音可以在创造它们的身体消失很久之后继续与我们交谈。

paras.en: I read a poignant post online written by a guy who had lost his dad after years of dementia. He missed his dad’s voice, he wrote, so he cloned it. He paid for the starter pack, submitted three minutes of his dad’s audio, and he wrote, quote, a few minutes later, I had a scarily accurate clone of my dead father’s voice. He goes on to write, quote, my family and I had a good cathartic cry upon hearing the results. I had his cloned voice read the Lord’s Prayer as well as ‘Twas the Night before Christmas. Just hearing his simulated voice again is such a blessing and is helping me in the grief process. End quote.
paras.zh: 我在网上读到一篇令人心酸的帖子，作者是一位因多年痴呆症而失去父亲的人。他写道，他想念父亲的声音，所以他克隆了它。他支付了入门包的费用，提交了三分钟的他父亲的音频，然后他写道，几分钟后，我就得到了我已故父亲的声音的极其准确的克隆。他继续写道，引用，我和我的家人在听到结果后哭了一场。我让他的克隆声音朗读了主祷文以及《这是圣诞节前夜》。再次听到他的模拟声音真是一件幸事，并且正在帮助我度过悲伤的过程。结束报价。

paras.en: There are lots of companies now offering this exact thing. A casual search online gets me to a company that sells chats with dead loved ones. There’s a big orange button to click that says bring them back to life. A 2024 documentary called “Eternal You” follows the stories of people as they grapple with this idea. Here’s a little bit of the trailer.
paras.zh: 现在有很多公司提供这种产品。在网上随意搜索，我找到了一家销售与已故亲人聊天的公司。有一个橙色的大按钮可以点击，上面写着让它们复活。一部 2024 年的纪录片《永恒的你》讲述了人们与这个想法作斗争的故事。这是预告片的一小部分。

paras.en: [Audio] We are on the verge of a new era. Hi. It’s like, it’s the funniest thing. It’s like, what’s the first thing you say to someone that’s dead? Like, welcome back.
paras.zh: [音频]我们正处于新时代的边缘。你好。就像，这是最有趣的事情。就像，你对死去的人说的第一句话是什么？就像，欢迎回来。

paras.en: Sanders: Griefbots or digital avatars of loved ones offer a bridge from the past to the present, a way to remember vividly. But they are also a denial, of sorts, that all life must come to an end.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：悲伤机器人或亲人的数字化身提供了从过去到现在的桥梁，是一种生动地记住的方式。但它们也在某种程度上否认所有生命都必须结束。

paras.en: [Audio] And what I can tell you is that AI really is changing the way that we interact with death.
paras.zh: [音频]我可以告诉你的是，人工智能确实正在改变我们与死亡互动的​​方式。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s from a 2025 TEDx talk from Dylan Thomas Doyle. He’s a former hospital chaplain, current academic researcher at Northwestern University and self-described philosophy bro. His work explores death and AI.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是迪伦·托马斯·道尔 2025 年 TEDx 演讲中的内容。他曾是一名医院牧师，现任西北大学学术研究员，自称是哲学兄弟。他的作品探索死亡和人工智能。

paras.en: [Audio] Imagine that you are at a funeral, and you’re sitting there in silent reflection, and all of a sudden, on the back screen in the auditorium, a woman’s face appears. And it’s the face of a woman named Marina. And her hologram, she starts talking to you, and she starts asking you how you’re doing today. And you answer her, and then you ask her a question back. And she responds as if she is still there.
paras.zh: [音频]想象一下，你正在参加一场葬礼，你坐在那里默默地沉思，突然，礼堂的后屏幕上出现了一张女人的脸。这是一个名叫玛丽娜的女人的脸。和她的全息图，她开始和你说话，她开始问你今天过得怎么样。你回答她，然后你反问她一个问题。她的反应就好像她还在那里一样。

paras.en: Sanders: I called Doyle to ask about the implications of using technology this way.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我打电话给多伊尔询问以这种方式使用技术的影响。

paras.en: Doyle: It was on my radar as a chaplain and a technology researcher, I started thinking through, well, what is the actual impact of this technology on people? So what is it like to hear the voice, in the context of this podcast, the voice of, say, your father who’s passed away while you’re actively grieving their death? And they’re not just repeating what they said or a journal entry in their voice, but like, creating new stories and new relationships through their voice. It gives a lot of people existential ick, is what I’ve heard. And that’s something that I really, I’m curious about.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：作为一名牧师和技术研究员，我开始思考这项技术对人们的实际影响是什么？那么，在这个播客的背景下，听到你的父亲的声音，比如说，当你正在积极哀悼他们的死亡时，听到他去世的声音是什么感觉？他们不仅仅是用自己的声音重复自己所说的话或日记条目，而是通过自己的声音创造新的故事和新的关系。据我所知，它让很多人感到厌恶。这确实是我很好奇的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: There’s tension here, Doyle tells me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔告诉我，这里存在紧张局势。

paras.en: Doyle: So there’s this push force where you’re like, this is not right. We don’t have the narrative or cultural script to understand what’s going on there. But then as people are beginning to use it, there’s a comfort that comes out of it. So we’re working in that tension space between this comfort that comes, then you’re still dealing with this push away from this technology of it just being weird in a way that people are still grappling with language, I think, to describe.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：所以你会觉得有一种推力，这是不对的。我们没有叙事或文化脚本来理解那里正在发生的事情。但当人们开始使用它时，就会产生一种安慰。因此，我们正在这种即将到来的舒适感之间的紧张空间中工作，然后你仍然在处理这种远离这项技术的情况，它只是以一种奇怪的方式，我认为，人们仍在努力用语言来描述。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s not clear how these types of interactions might affect grieving. They could help or they could hurt.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：目前尚不清楚这些类型的互动如何影响悲伤。他们可能会提供帮助，也可能会造成伤害。

paras.en: Doyle: There is this tension between more healthy continuing bonds. So continuing that relationship by, say, writing letters to your dead loved one or, you know, talking out loud to them and continuing that relationship in a positive way that moves us through a healthy grief process and a grief journey. Or hanging on to our relationship with that person to a degree where we can’t actually do any sort of moving on.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：更健康的持续关系之间存在着这种紧张关系。因此，通过给死去的亲人写信，或者大声地与他们交谈，以积极的方式继续这种关系，让我们度过一个健康的悲伤过程和悲伤之旅，来继续这种关系。或者我们紧紧抓住与那个人的关系，以至于我们实际上无法采取任何行动。

paras.en: Sanders: Doyle points out that we don’t have good data on how many people might be using griefbots.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔指出，我们没有关于有多少人可能使用悲伤机器人的良好数据。

paras.en: Doyle: I just don’t want us to get ahead of ourselves when it comes to people like using these. So the capability to do everything we’ve talked about with griefbots is there. But the actual use cases of individuals in their homes using this, it’s still pretty unclear about the adoption of those technologies.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：我只是不想让我们在谈到喜欢使用这些的人时表现得超前。因此，悲伤机器人有能力完成我们谈到的所有事情。但个人在家中使用该技术的实际用例，这些技术的采用情况仍然相当不清楚。

paras.en: Sanders: But even if griefbots aren’t widespread, the questions they raise aren’t going away. These voices are blurring the lines between a memory and a present-day experience, between alive and dead. Here’s Karina Nagin again.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但即使悲伤机器人并不普遍，它们提出的问题也不会消失。这些声音模糊了记忆与当下经历、生与死之间的界限。卡琳娜·纳金又来了。

paras.en: Nagin: It’s an interesting conversation that we’re having right now of what happens to your voice once you pass away. Some people are starting to integrate this into their wills or their sort of final wishes of, do you want your voice to be able to speak at your own memorial service?
paras.zh: 纳金：我们现在正在进行一场有趣的对话，内容是关于你去世后你的声音会发生什么。有些人开始将其融入他们的遗嘱或最终愿望中，你希望你的声音能够在你自己的追悼会上发言吗？

paras.en: Do you want to have messages saved in your voice that are for your child at graduation that they listen to? Who and when can use that? I think that these are things that people are starting to think about. Who owns your voice? Can your children use your voice to write a speech for their children’s graduation? Or do you want that voice to be deleted once you pass away? Very tricky questions.
paras.zh: 您是否想在您的声音中保存留言供您的孩子在毕业典礼上聆听？谁以及何时可以使用它？我认为这些是人们开始思考的事情。谁拥有你的声音？您的孩子可以用您的声音为孩子的毕业典礼写演讲稿吗？或者你希望在你去世后删除那个声音？非常棘手的问题。

paras.en: Sanders: Rules about who can use voice clones are all over the place. Regulations vary by state and by country, and even companies have their own individual policies in place. There are no clear guidelines, and that makes sense given how young this technology is. Conversations about digital voices and how to use them are inherently very personal. There are as many different takes as there are people. I asked MA if she and Jules had talked about this.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于谁可以使用语音克隆的规则无处不在。法规因州和国家而异，甚至公司也有自己的个人政策。目前还没有明确的指导方针，考虑到这项技术还很年轻，这是有道理的。关于数字语音以及如何使用它们的对话本质上是非常个人化的。有多少人，就有多少种不同的看法。我问妈妈她和朱尔斯是否谈过这件事。

paras.en: MA: I love that question. Both of us love this question because it’s so important. And we talked about it before he got the trache. Like when he was already using the voice, we were talking about different things in bed at night. And he said, you know, I have a very clear request that my voice like dies with me, basically, that, you know, I ask that you don’t use the voice to keep me alive in any way, that there’s no… And I was like, 100 percent clear. I hadn’t even thought about that. But yeah, it would make sense to be like, I miss him so much. I want to, whatever or. But no, as far as we’re concerned, his voice dies when he does. And his voice will live on in whatever videos or things we captured, whatever he’s left us intentionally. And that’s as far as that goes.
paras.zh: MA：我喜欢这个问题。我们俩都喜欢这个问题，因为它非常重要。在他接受气管切开术之前我们就讨论过这件事。就像当他已经使用这个声音时，我们晚上在床上谈论不同的事情。他说，你知道，我有一个非常明确的要求，我的声音会随着我一起消失，基本上，你知道，我要求你不要以任何方式使用声音让我活下去，没有……我的感觉是百分百清楚。我什至没有想到这一点。但是，是的，我非常想念他，这是有道理的。我想要，无论如何。但不，就我们而言，当他这样做时，他的声音就消失了。他的声音将永远存在于我们拍摄的任何视频或事物中，无论他故意留给我们什么。就这样了。

paras.en: Sanders: So when Jules is gone, his voice will be gone too. But right now is a different story.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以当朱尔斯去世时，他的声音也会消失。但现在情况不同了。

paras.en: MA: Well back in 2021, I was writing an Instagram post about something. It was him playing with Skylar in the backyard while he was already like, you know, had trouble with everything, but he was doing what he could. And I asked him like, you know, what, what do you want to caption it? And he just said that, right here, right now phrase, something else, and like right here, right now. And it became our family mantra. It became something that we wanted to just to share and in both a sense of like do the things that you want to do.
paras.zh: MA：早在 2021 年，我就在 Instagram 上写了一篇关于某事的帖子。那是他和斯凯拉在后院玩耍，而他已经好像，你知道，一切都遇到了麻烦，但他正在尽力而为。我问他，你知道，你想给它加上什么标题吗？他只是说，就在这里，现在，短语，其他的东西，就像就在这里，现在。这成了我们家庭的座右铭。它成为我们想要分享的东西，从某种意义上说，就像做你想做的事情。

paras.en: And also something that’s always been big for Jules that I’ve admired him articulate is that it’s not just about, oh, just go forward and do all the things and like suck the marrow out of life. It’s like just also, like, settle. Like it doesn’t have to be that extreme, you know. There’s a beautiful thing about that presence and that settling in. And again, with ALS being something where you’re given the diagnosis, which is terminal, it’s basically a death sentence. Most people are given, you know, two to five years. You don’t know where you’re going to fall in that. We’ve known people that have passed away in a year and a half. We’ve known people that are six years in like Jules, but can still kind of walk around, speak a little bit. ALS touches everybody really differently. So you really don’t know what’s coming. And there’s a lot of like forward thinking that you can do that detaches you from being in your life. So how are you here? And then there’s a lot of backwards, you know, reminiscing and grieving about all the things we’ve lost and how we wish things were different. But then that also takes you out of like this moment right now and this part of your story.
paras.zh: 对朱尔斯来说，我很钦佩他能表达出来的一直很重要的一点是，这不仅仅是，哦，继续前进，做所有的事情，就像从生活中吸取骨髓一样。这就像也，就像，安顿下来。你知道，事情不必那么极端。这种存在和安定下来是一件美好的事情。再说一次，当你被诊断出 ALS 时，这是晚期的，基本上就等于被判了死刑。你知道，大多数人都会被给予两到五年的时间。你不知道自己会陷入其中。我们认识一年半内去世的人。我们认识像朱尔斯这样六岁的人，但仍然可以四处走动，说一点话。 ALS 对每个人的影响确实不同。所以你真的不知道会发生什么。你可以做很多类似的前瞻性思考，让你脱离生活。那么你在这里怎么样？然后有很多倒退，你知道，回忆和悲伤我们失去的所有东西，以及我们如何希望事情有所不同。但这也会让你脱离现在的这一刻和故事的这一部分。

paras.en: Sanders: This part of the story is the important part. Right here, right now.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：故事的这一部分是重要的部分。就在这里，就是现在。

paras.en: On the next and final episode of The Deep End, Talk to Me. We’re going to look at what’s next for Jules and Casey and what’s next for the science racing to give voices back to people.
paras.zh: 在《深渊》的下一集也是最后一集中，《跟我说话》。我们将看看朱尔斯和凯西的下一步是什么，以及科学竞赛的下一步是什么，以回馈人们的声音。

paras.en: Vikash Gilja: We can see all the pieces coming together. All of the emphasis, capital, quite frankly, talent focused on advancing AI techniques and technologies. You know, our little corner can benefit from it, right? These tools weren’t available even five years ago.
paras.zh: Vikash Gilja：我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。所有的重点、资本、坦率地说、人才都集中在推进人工智能技术和技术上。你知道，我们的小角落可以从中受益，对吗？这些工具在五年前还没有出现。

paras.en: Sanders: What’s next for the human voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人声的下一步是什么？

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: Sanders: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：深渊是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.zh: 声音来源：Garuda1982 的《春天有自行车和乌鸦的城市公园》、kyles 的印刷机纺轮.flac、AudioSea 的 Turning Pages 01.wav。

articles.title: Eating Blueberries Every Day Could Reduce Depressive Symptoms in Older Adults
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: There's a lot of goodness packed inside the fruits we eat, and scientists continue to look at how that goodness might benefit our mental as well as our physical health.
paras.zh: 我们吃的水果中含有很多好处，科学家们继续研究这些好处如何有益于我们的心理和身体健康。

paras.en: In a small pilot study, researchers led by a team at Harvard Medical School in the US found hints that a daily dose of blueberries may help ease the symptoms of depression in older, sedentary adults.
paras.zh: 在一项小型试点研究中，由美国哈佛医学院的一个团队领导的研究人员发现，每日服用蓝莓可能有助于缓解久坐的老年人的抑郁症状。

paras.en: This is a group of people who we already know are at a higher risk of depression, and who don't necessarily have easy access to some of the natural ways of tackling it – including exercising and getting outdoors.
paras.zh: 我们已经知道这一群人患抑郁症的风险较高，而且他们不一定能轻松获得一些自然的方法来应对抑郁症，包括锻炼和户外活动。

paras.en: Eating blueberries every day might be a simple, healthy way of keeping depression at bay.
paras.zh: 每天吃蓝莓可能是预防抑郁症的一种简单而健康的方法。

paras.en: The researchers have now published their work in the Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging, and the study showed some interesting gut bacteria shifts caused by the extra blueberries too.
paras.zh: 研究人员现已在《营养、健康和衰老杂志》上发表了他们的研究成果，研究表明额外的蓝莓也会引起一些有趣的肠道细菌变化。

paras.en: "Our objective was to preliminarily determine the effect of blueberry consumption on the gut microbiome, metabolites, and depressive symptoms," says molecular nutritionist Courtney Millar, from Harvard Medical School.
paras.zh: 哈佛医学院的分子营养学家考特尼·米勒 (Courtney Millar) 表示：“我们的目标是初步确定食用蓝莓对肠道微生物组、代谢物和抑郁症状的影响。”

paras.en: The study involved 18 participants aged 65 and older, who were either given 48 grams of freeze-dried blueberry powder every day (about two cups' worth of berries) or the same amount of placebo powder.
paras.zh: 该研究涉及 18 名 65 岁及以上的参与者，他们每天服用 48 克冻干蓝莓粉（约两杯浆果）或等量的安慰剂粉。

paras.en: After three months, depressive symptoms had improved in both groups. Those in the blueberry group showed bigger and more consistent improvements, though the difference didn't reach statistical significance.
paras.zh: 三个月后，两组的抑郁症状都有所改善。蓝莓组的受试者表现出更大、更一致的改善，但差异并未达到统计学显着性。

paras.en: "While changes in mental well-being outcomes are not different between groups, they appear to be 'improvements' of stronger magnitude in the blueberry group, with less variability compared to the placebo group," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“虽然各组之间心理健康结果的变化没有差异，但蓝莓组的‘改善’幅度似乎更大，且与安慰剂组相比变异性更小。”

paras.en: "This pilot study was designed to test intervention feasibility and gather the preliminary data on outcomes that are needed to estimate power of a larger trial."
paras.zh: “这项试点研究旨在测试干预的可行性，并收集估计更大规模试验功效所需的初步数据。”

paras.en: In terms of gut bacteria, there were some small changes in the enzymes (proteins triggering chemical reactions) present in the blueberry participants.
paras.zh: 就肠道细菌而言，蓝莓参与者体内的酶（引发化学反应的蛋白质）发生了一些微小的变化。

paras.en: Six types of bacterial enzyme genes changed in abundance, five of them rising, including one involved in making gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a neurotransmitter previously linked to depression.
paras.zh: 六种类型的细菌酶基因发生了丰富的变化，其中五种增加了，其中一种涉及制造γ-氨基丁酸（GABA），这是一种先前与抑郁症有关的神经递质。

paras.en: It's already well-established that fiber and anthocyanins (blue pigments) in blueberries can have an effect on the gut microbiome, so some shifts were expected – and a more detailed analysis will be needed to confirm exactly what's going on.
paras.zh: 众所周知，蓝莓中的纤维和花青素（蓝色色素）会对肠道微生物组产生影响，因此预计会发生一些变化，并且需要更详细的分析来确切确认到底发生了什么。

paras.en: The researchers also acknowledge the relatively small sample size here, and that the participants were mostly female and white, with mild depressive symptoms rather than diagnosed depression.
paras.zh: 研究人员还承认，这里的样本量相对较小，而且参与者大多是女性和白人，有轻微的抑郁症状，而不是被诊断为抑郁症。

paras.en: While we can't make any grand conclusions from the results published here, it sets the stage for bigger studies.
paras.zh: 虽然我们无法从这里发表的结果得出任何重大结论，但它为更大规模的研究奠定了基础。

paras.en: The researchers say further studies should involve more diverse populations and "recruit a larger sample size to account for the effect of potential confounders and baseline differences."
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，进一步的研究应该涉及更多不同的人群，并“招募更大的样本量来解释潜在混杂因素和基线差异的影响。”

paras.en: That there was no statistically significant difference between the blueberry and placebo group might make you think there's nothing to see here – but the bigger, more consistent improvements in symptoms, coupled with the gut microbiome shifts, are reasons to run follow-up studies.
paras.zh: 蓝莓组和安慰剂组之间没有统计学上的显着差异，可能会让你认为这里没有什么可看的——但症状的更大、更一致的改善，加上肠道微生物组的变化，是进行后续研究的理由。

paras.en: We also know that the placebo effect has been shown in study after study. You could argue that even the thought of a daily dose of blueberry powder was enough to lift the moods of the placebo group participants.
paras.zh: 我们还知道，安慰剂效应已在一项又一项的研究中得到证实。你可能会说，即使是每天服用一剂蓝莓粉的想法也足以改善安慰剂组参与者的情绪。

paras.en: The brain and the gut have a complex, two-way relationship that scientists are still trying to understand. There's already some notable evidence that what we eat in our diets can have an effect on mental health, and this small study adds to it.
paras.zh: 大脑和肠道之间存在着复杂的双向关系，科学家们仍在试图理解这一关系。已经有一些显着的证据表明，我们饮食中所吃的东西会对心理健康产生影响，这项小型研究进一步证实了这一点。

paras.en: "Our data are preliminary and warrant additional studies to investigate the link between blueberries, the gut microbiome, and mood in older adults," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们的数据是初步的，需要进行更多的研究来调查蓝莓、肠道微生物组和老年人情绪之间的联系。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《营养、健康与衰老杂志》上。

articles.title: 2 Words in an Overlooked Flight Log Reveal a Chilling Detail About The Hiroshima Bombing
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: At 8.15 in the morning of 6 August 1945, the gates to hell opened on the Japanese city of Hiroshima when the US military unleashed the nuclear bomb.
paras.zh: 1945年8月6日上午8点15分，美军发射了核弹，日本广岛市的地狱之门打开了。

paras.en: As tens of thousands of people died on the ground below, the American bomber Enola Gay that dropped the warhead soared away. Meanwhile, a growing cloud of soot and smoke began to billow up from the firestorm that raged in the wake of the devastating detonation.
paras.zh: 随着数万人死在下面的地面上，投下弹头的美国轰炸机埃诺拉·盖伊翱翔而去。与此同时，毁灭性爆炸后肆虐的大火开始冒出越来越多的烟灰和烟雾。

paras.en: Just 97 minutes later, at 10.52 am Tinian time, navigator Theodore Van Kirk made a brief entry in the aircraft's flight log in scrawled uppercase letters.
paras.zh: 仅仅 97 分钟后，即天宁岛时间上午 10 点 52 分，领航员西奥多·范·柯克 (Theodore Van Kirk) 在飞机的飞行日志中用潦草的大写字母做了简短的记录。

paras.en: That tiny, overlooked detail has now given scientists a new window into the world's only nuclear firestorm on record.
paras.zh: 这个被忽视的微小细节现在为科学家们提供了了解世界上有记录以来唯一的核火灾风暴的新窗口。

paras.en: According to a paper led by atmospheric scientist David Romps of the University of California, Berkeley, that note suggests that the plume of soot had risen at least 11.3 kilometers (7 miles) into the sky.
paras.zh: 根据加州大学伯克利分校大气科学家 David Romps 领导的一篇论文，该说明表明烟尘羽流已上升到天空至少 11.3 公里（7 英里）。

paras.en: "The Hiroshima firestorm lofted soot well into the upper troposphere, consistent with nuclear-winter scenarios," the team writes in a paper published in Geophysical Research Letters.
paras.zh: 研究小组在《地球物理研究快报》上发表的一篇论文中写道：“广岛大火将烟灰带入了对流层上层，这与核冬天的情况一致。”

paras.en: The aftermath of a nuclear bomb is chaos. The explosion itself and its mushroom cloud are over relatively quickly, but the intense heat the explosion generates can create a furious storm of fires that rampages for hours.
paras.zh: The aftermath of a nuclear bomb is chaos.爆炸本身及其蘑菇云相对较快地结束，但爆炸产生的强烈热量可能会引发猛烈的火灾风暴，持续数小时。

paras.en: As the fires lit by the explosion of the Little Boy atomic bomb spread and merged across Hiroshima, the blazing temperatures generated powerful updrafts that carried smoke and soot high into the atmosphere, forming a towering column of cloud.
paras.zh: 当小男孩原子弹爆炸引发的大火在广岛蔓延并融合时，炽热的温度产生了强大的上升气流，将烟雾和烟灰带入高空大气层，形成了高耸的云柱。

paras.en: Just how high that cloud can rise is crucial to understanding the consequences of nuclear warfare.
paras.zh: 云层能升到多高对于理解核战争的后果至关重要。

paras.en: If enough soot reaches the stratosphere, it can linger for months or years, blocking sunlight and cooling the planet below.
paras.zh: 如果足够多的烟尘到达平流层，它可能会停留数月或数年，阻挡阳光并冷却下面的行星。

paras.en: In a large-scale nuclear conflict, the cumulative effects of many such fires could trigger a nuclear winter, with potentially catastrophic consequences for agriculture and food supplies around the world.
paras.zh: 在大规模核冲突中，许多此类火灾的累积影响可能会引发核冬天，给世界各地的农业和粮食供应带来潜在的灾难性后果。

paras.en: But some scientists have disagreed about whether nuclear firestorms can carry soot high enough. Some simulations suggest that most soot would remain in the lower atmosphere, where rain could wash it out before it had a lasting effect on the global climate.
paras.zh: 但一些科学家对于核火焰风暴是否能够将烟尘带到足够高的高度存在分歧。一些模拟表明，大多数烟尘将留在低层大气中，在对全球气候产生持久影响之前，雨水可以将其冲走。

paras.en: The problem here – and thankfully so – is that we have very few real-world observations of nuclear firestorms. In fact, the bombing of Hiroshima is the only known instance; none eventuated from the bombing of Nagasaki three days later.
paras.zh: 这里的问题是——值得庆幸的是——我们对现实世界中的核火灾风暴的观察很少。事实上，广岛原子弹爆炸是唯一已知的例子。三天后对长崎的轰炸没有造成任何后果。

paras.en: Previous researchers have tried to reconstruct the height of the Hiroshima plume using historical photographs, but the results relied on several uncertainties.
paras.zh: 之前的研究人员曾尝试使用历史照片重建广岛羽流的高度，但结果依赖于一些不确定性。

paras.en: Romps and his colleagues, however, found another source of evidence in the historical record.
paras.zh: 然而，朗普斯和他的同事在历史记录中发现了另一个证据来源。

paras.en: And their calculation is stunningly clever.
paras.zh: 而且他们的计算是惊人的聪明。

paras.en: The movements of Enola Gay that day are documented in detail, almost down to the minute. When Van Kirk noted "CLOUD GONE" at 97 minutes after the detonation, the plane was an estimated 750 to 764 kilometers away, at an altitude of around 7,440 meters (24,400 feet).
paras.zh: 埃诺拉·盖伊那天的一举一动都被详细记录下来，几乎精确到分钟。当范柯克在爆炸后 97 分钟注意到“云消失”时，飞机估计距离 750 至 764 公里，高度约为 7,440 米（24,400 英尺）。

paras.en: And that suggests that the cloud was not quite so gone as the log indicates, but that, from their position, the crew could no longer see it.
paras.zh: 这表明云层并没有像日志中显示的那样消失，但从机组人员的位置来看，他们再也看不到它了。

paras.en: A separate military memorandum recorded that the crew's "observation was then limited by haze and not curvature of the Earth."
paras.zh: 一份单独的军事备忘录记录称，机组人员的“观察受到雾霾而非地球曲率的限制”。

paras.en: That means that the cloud had not dipped below the horizon. It was obscured instead by atmospheric haze.
paras.zh: 这意味着云层并未沉入地平线以下。相反，它被大气雾霾遮蔽了。

paras.en: This distinction is key – because if the cloud was still above the horizon from such a vast distance, then it must have been extraordinarily tall.
paras.zh: 这种区别很关键——因为如果距离这么远，云仍然位于地平线上方，那么它一定非常高。

paras.en: So, by calculating how far the crew could have seen from their altitude, the researchers could work backward to determine the minimum height of the plume.
paras.zh: 因此，通过计算机组人员从他们的高度可以看到的距离，研究人员可以逆向确定羽流的最小高度。

paras.en: But this isn't necessarily straightforward, either.
paras.zh: 但这也不一定是简单的。

paras.en: Light doesn't travel through Earth's atmosphere in perfectly straight lines. As air density changes with altitude, light bends slightly toward the surface, allowing us to see a little farther around Earth's curvature than geometry alone would suggest.
paras.zh: 光不会以完美的直线穿过地球大气层。由于空气密度随着高度的变化而变化，光线会稍微向地表弯曲，这使我们能够在地球曲率周围看到比仅靠几何学所建议的更远的距离。

paras.en: Accounting for this required the researchers to reconstruct the atmospheric conditions on the day of the bombing.
paras.zh: 考虑到这一点，研究人员需要重建爆炸当天的大气条件。

paras.en: Using three historical weather reconstructions, they estimated how temperature and air pressure changed with altitude, allowing them to calculate how light would have bent through the atmosphere that day.
paras.zh: 利用三个历史天气重建，他们估计了温度和气压如何随高度变化，从而使他们能够计算出当天光线如何穿过大气层。

paras.en: They then ran 100,000 simulations to account for uncertainties in the aircraft's position, altitude, and the atmospheric conditions.
paras.zh: 然后，他们进行了 100,000 次模拟，以解释飞机位置、高度和大气条件的不确定性。

paras.en: This, obviously, still leaves a not insignificant degree of uncertainty.
paras.zh: 显然，这仍然留下了相当大的不确定性。

paras.en: But even so, the researchers calculated with 95 percent confidence that the plume must have reached a minimum height of 11.3 kilometers – consistent with nuclear winter scenarios.
paras.zh: 但即便如此，研究人员仍以 95% 的置信度计算出，烟羽的最低高度必须达到 11.3 公里，这与核冬天的情景相符。

paras.en: Now, the Hiroshima bombing did not cause nuclear winter. But nuclear winter is not expected to result from a single explosion. Rather, it is the potential cumulative consequence of vast amounts of soot injected into the atmosphere by multiple nuclear firestorms ignited during a nuclear war.
paras.zh: 现在，广岛原子弹爆炸并没有造成核冬天。但核冬天预计不会由一次爆炸造成。相反，它是核战争期间引发的多次核风暴向大气中注入大量烟灰的潜在累积后果。

paras.en: What Hiroshima shows is that nuclear firestorms can loft soot to altitudes relevant to this concept – an important piece of evidence consistent with the possibility of nuclear winter.
paras.zh: 广岛表明，核火灾风暴可以将烟灰提升到与这一概念相关的高度——这是与核冬天可能性相一致的重要证据。

paras.en: Let us truly hope the world never has to find out the hard way.
paras.zh: 让我们真诚地希望世界永远不必经历艰难的道路。

paras.en: The research has been published in Geophysical Research Letters.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《地球物理研究快报》上。

articles.title: Scientists Discover a Potential Driver of Aging in The Testicles
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: The ovaries aren't the only sex organs with a biological clock.
paras.zh: 卵巢并不是唯一具有生物钟的性器官。

paras.en: Testicles also show signs of aging – with altered hormone levels, DNA damage, and reduced sperm function over time.
paras.zh: 睾丸还显示出衰老的迹象——随着时间的推移，激素水平发生改变、DNA 损伤以及精子功能下降。

paras.en: Yet despite their importance to human reproduction, it's not yet fully understood why testicles age, or what makes their biological clock tick.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管睾丸对人类生殖很重要，但人们尚未完全了解睾丸为何会衰老，或者是什么让它们的生物钟运转。

paras.en: Researchers in China have recently discovered a molecule that may speed up the aging process.
paras.zh: 中国研究人员最近发现了一种可能加速衰老过程的分子。

paras.en: The team first collected testicular tissues from two young donors, aged 23 and 30, and two older donors, aged 62 and 91 – all of whom had already fathered children and had a testicle removed for medical reasons.
paras.zh: 研究小组首先从两名年龄分别为 23 岁和 30 岁的年轻捐赠者和两名年龄分别为 62 岁和 91 岁的老年捐赠者收集了睾丸组织，他们都已经是孩子的父亲，并因医疗原因切除了睾丸。

paras.en: After analyzing more than 10,000 cell nuclei, the scientists found significant differences between young and old participants.
paras.zh: 在分析了 10,000 多个细胞核后，科学家们发现年轻和年老参与者之间存在显着差异。

paras.en: "With advancing age, the testis undergoes profound structural alterations," explain the authors in their published paper, led by researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Naval Medical University of China.
paras.zh: “随着年龄的增长，睾丸会发生深刻的结构变化，”由中国科学院和中国海军军医大学的研究人员领导的论文作者在其发表的论文中解释道。

paras.en: The sample size is small, but in the lab, when researchers increased the expression of a single gene in cultured testicular cells, it accelerated signs of aging.
paras.zh: 样本量很小，但在实验室中，当研究人员增加培养的睾丸细胞中单个基因的表达时，它加速了衰老的迹象。

paras.en: The findings are published in the Journal of Molecular Cell Biology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《分子细胞生物学杂志》上。

paras.en: Unlike the ovaries, which contain a finite supply of immature eggs, the testicle contains self-renewing stem cells associated with sperm production.
paras.zh: 与含有有限供应的未成熟卵子的卵巢不同，睾丸含有与精子产生相关的自我更新干细胞。

paras.en: This means that a bank of sperm-producing cells can be maintained even into older age.
paras.zh: 这意味着精子生成细胞库甚至可以维持到老年。

paras.en: While it's true that men can father children past age 60, that does not mean male fertility remains constant throughout life. Cells in the testicle still show signs of aging.
paras.zh: 虽然男性确实可以在 60 岁以上生孩子，但这并不意味着男性的生育能力在一生中保持不变。睾丸细胞仍然显示出衰老的迹象。

paras.en: After age 45, for instance, sperm quality and function tend to decline, though not quite as precipitously as egg quantity and quality in the ovaries.
paras.zh: 例如，45 岁之后，精子的质量和功能往往会下降，尽管不像卵巢中卵子的数量和质量那样急剧下降。

paras.en: In the past, research on testicular tissue has identified two cell types that decline with age: Sertoli cells, which support sperm production, and Leydig cells, which produce testosterone.
paras.zh: 过去，对睾丸组织的研究发现了两种随着年龄增长而衰退的细胞类型：支持精子产生的支持细胞和产生睾酮的间质细胞。

paras.en: Both of these cells communicate closely with one another.
paras.zh: 这两种细胞彼此密切沟通。

paras.en: With age, however, this new research suggests their signaling may break down.
paras.zh: 然而，这项新研究表明，随着年龄的增长，它们的信号传导可能会崩溃。

paras.en: "We observed a widespread dysregulation in cell–cell interactions involving aging Sertoli cells and Leydig cells," the authors of the recent study write.
paras.zh: 最近研究的作者写道：“我们观察到细胞间相互作用存在广泛的失调，涉及衰老的支持细胞和间质细胞。”

paras.en: This could be detrimental to sperm development.
paras.zh: 这可能不利于精子的发育。

paras.en: With age, researchers found that Leydig cells show significant changes in their interactions related to hormone secretion and blood vessel formation.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，随着年龄的增长，间质细胞与激素分泌和血管形成相关的相互作用表现出显着变化。

paras.en: They also found that Sertoli cells communicate differently with immune cells.
paras.zh: 他们还发现支持细胞与免疫细胞的沟通方式不同。

paras.en: Perhaps most strikingly, researchers noticed Sertoli cells in older testicles expressed significantly more of a protein called WLS.
paras.zh: 也许最引人注目的是，研究人员注意到老年睾丸中的支持细胞明显更多地表达一种名为 WLS 的蛋白质。

paras.en: In the lab, when the team increased WLS expression in cultured Sertoli cells, it accelerated signs of aging.
paras.zh: 在实验室中，当研究小组增加培养的支持细胞中的 WLS 表达时，它加速了衰老的迹象。

paras.en: The findings suggest this may not just be a marker of aging; it may also be a driver of aging.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，这可能不仅仅是衰老的标志，也是衰老的标志。它也可能是衰老的一个驱动因素。

paras.en: "As a Wnt transporter," the authors explain, "WLS is central to the Wnt signaling pathway that governs stem cell self-renewal, differentiation, metabolism, survival, and proliferation… Despite its established roles, the specific function of WLS in testicular aging remains unclear."
paras.zh: “作为一种 Wnt 转运蛋白，”作者解释道，“WLS 是 Wnt 信号通路的核心，控制干细胞的自我更新、分化、代谢、存活和增殖……尽管其作用已确定，但 WLS 在睾丸衰老中的具体功能仍不清楚。”

paras.en: The findings are consistent with previous reports showing changes in Sertoli and Leydig cells with age and offer new avenues for future research.
paras.zh: 这些发现与之前的报告一致，显示支持细胞和间质细胞随着年龄的变化而变化，并为未来的研究提供了新的途径。

paras.en: But studies like these are few and far between.
paras.zh: 但像这样的研究却少之又少。

paras.en: "The availability of high-quality human testicular tissue samples, especially from older individuals, is limited due to ethical considerations and practical constraints," writes the research team.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“由于伦理考虑和实际限制，高质量人类睾丸组织样本的可用性，特别是来自老年人的样本，受到限制。”

paras.en: "To improve the credibility and generalizability of our findings, more testis tissue samples need to be collected."
paras.zh: “为了提高我们研究结果的可信度和普遍性，需要收集更多的睾丸组织样本。”

paras.en: Other scientists agree we need more research on testicular tissue and its impact on male fertility.
paras.zh: 其他科学家一致认为，我们需要对睾丸组织及其对男性生育能力的影响进行更多研究。

paras.en: In 2023, an international consortium of experts, led by the University of Melbourne's Moira O'Bryan, called on governments and health systems to improve research on male infertility.
paras.zh: 2023 年，由墨尔本大学莫伊拉·奥布莱恩 (Moira O'Bryan) 领导的国际专家联盟呼吁各国政府和卫生系统改进对男性不育症的研究。

paras.en: The consortium recommended creating a global biobank of tissues and clinical data to help researchers understand the various causes of infertility.
paras.zh: 该联盟建议创建一个全球组织和临床数据生物库，以帮助研究人员了解不孕的各种原因。

paras.en: "For most infertile men, the cause of their infertility is unknown. When it is known, few targeted treatments exist," explained O'Bryan in 2023.
paras.zh: 奥布莱恩在 2023 年解释说：“对于大多数不孕男性来说，他们不孕的原因尚不清楚。即使知道原因，也很少有针对性的治疗方法。”

paras.en: The result is that women are often left to shoulder the burden of invasive fertility treatments like in vitro fertilization (IVF).
paras.zh: 结果是，女性常常不得不承担体外受精 (IVF) 等侵入性生育治疗的负担。

paras.en: Knowing more about the male biological clock could help level the playing field.
paras.zh: 更多地了解男性生物钟有助于创造公平的竞争环境。

paras.en: The research has been published in the Journal of Molecular Cell Biology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《分子细胞生物学杂志》上。

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to autism's origins hidden in the placenta

paras.en: Scientists discover a surprising clue to autism's origins hidden in the placenta
paras.zh: 科学家在胎盘中发现了自闭症起源的惊人线索

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered an unexpected connection between inflammation during pregnancy, placental damage, and autism-like traits in male mice, while females appeared naturally protected. The discovery could help explain why autism is diagnosed more frequently in boys and reveal new opportunities for early intervention.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现雄性小鼠怀孕期间的炎症、胎盘损伤和自闭症样特征之间存在意想不到的联系，而雌性小鼠似乎自然受到保护。这一发现可能有助于解释为什么男孩更容易诊断出自闭症，并揭示早期干预的新机会。

paras.en: Scientists are still working to understand why autism develops. Genetics are known to play a major role, but researchers have also found that conditions during pregnancy can influence the likelihood of autism spectrum disorder.
paras.zh: 科学家们仍在努力了解自闭症发生的原因。众所周知，遗传学起着重要作用，但研究人员还发现，怀孕期间的状况也会影响自闭症谱系障碍的可能性。

paras.en: A new study from Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL) has uncovered a surprising connection between inflammation during pregnancy, changes in the placenta, and the development of autism-like traits in male mice. The findings suggest that certain developmental disruptions may begin much earlier than previously recognized, potentially offering new clues about autism's origins.
paras.zh: 冷泉港实验室 (CSHL) 的一项新研究发现，雄性小鼠怀孕期间的炎症、胎盘的变化和自闭症样特征的发展之间存在令人惊讶的联系。研究结果表明，某些发育障碍可能比之前认识的要早得多，这可能为自闭症的起源提供新的线索。

paras.en: "To truly understand autism spectrum disorder, we have to look beyond the brain," CSHL Associate Professor Lucas Cheadle says. "Our work suggests that maternal immune activation and changes within the placenta are a gateway to autism for some unique individuals."
paras.zh: CSHL 副教授 Lucas Cheadle 说：“要真正了解自闭症谱系障碍，我们必须超越大脑。” “我们的工作表明，母体免疫激活和胎盘内的变化是某些独特个体患自闭症的门户。”

paras.en: Scientists Identify an Early Window of Vulnerability
paras.zh: 科学家发现了脆弱性的早期窗口

paras.en: To investigate how inflammation affects fetal development, Cheadle and his colleagues triggered an immune response in pregnant mice at different stages of pregnancy. They used a substance that mimics the immune system's reaction to a viral infection without actually introducing a virus.
paras.zh: 为了研究炎症如何影响胎儿发育，钱德尔和他的同事在怀孕的不同阶段触发了怀孕小鼠的免疫反应。他们使用了一种模拟免疫系统对病毒感染的反应的物质，但实际上并没有引入病毒。

paras.en: The researchers discovered that mouse fetuses were especially vulnerable when inflammation occurred 12.5 days into pregnancy. According to Irene Sanchez Martin, a postdoctoral researcher in Cheadle's laboratory, approximately one-third of the fetuses showed developmental abnormalities within just 24 hours.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，当怀孕 12.5 天发生炎症时，小鼠胎儿特别容易受到伤害。 Cheadle 实验室的博士后研究员 Irene Sanchez Martin 表示，大约三分之一的胎儿在短短 24 小时内就出现了发育异常。

paras.en: Scientists have investigated the effects of maternal immune activation for decades, but these findings reveal signs of developmental disruption earlier than researchers had previously observed.
paras.zh: 几十年来，科学家们一直在研究母体免疫激活的影响，但这些发现揭示了发育中断的迹象，比研究人员之前观察到的更早。

paras.en: Even more striking was the difference between male and female fetuses. Across every experiment, autism-like traits appeared only in males, while females continued developing normally.
paras.zh: 更引人注目的是男性和女性胎儿之间的差异。在每项实验中，类似自闭症的特征仅出现在男性身上，而女性则继续正常发育。

paras.en: This unexpected distinction could provide insight into why autism is diagnosed substantially more often in boys than girls. What makes the finding especially intriguing is how early the difference appeared, before many of the biological changes normally associated with sex-specific development.
paras.zh: 这种意想不到的区别可以让我们深入了解为什么男孩比女孩更容易被诊断出自闭症。这一发现特别有趣的是这种差异出现的时间有多早，早于许多通常与性别特异性发育相关的生物学变化。

paras.en: "It's really fascinating, because we're looking at an age which precedes hormonal surges. It precedes sexual differentiation in the brain and many other regions. So, it's surprising there would be a sex-based difference this early."
paras.zh: “这真的很有趣，因为我们正在研究一个荷尔蒙激增之前的年龄。它早于大脑和许多其他区域的性别分化。因此，令人惊讶的是这么早就存在基于性别的差异。”

paras.en: A Surprising Connection Between the Placenta and Autism
paras.zh: 胎盘和自闭症之间令人惊讶的联系

paras.en: To determine why some developing mice were affected while others appeared protected, Cheadle and Sanchez Martin examined the placenta, the organ that connects a developing fetus to its mother and supports its growth throughout pregnancy.
paras.zh: 为了确定为什么一些发育中的老鼠受到影响，而另一些则似乎受到保护，钱德尔和桑切斯·马丁检查了胎盘，胎盘是将发育中的胎儿与其母亲连接起来并在整个怀孕期间支持其生长的器官。

paras.en: Their attention centered on specialized cells called spongiotrophoblasts, which occupy a region of the mouse placenta where maternal and fetal cells interact.
paras.zh: 他们的注意力集中在称为海绵滋养层的特殊细胞上，这些细胞占据了小鼠胎盘中母体和胎儿细胞相互作用的区域。

paras.en: In fetuses that developed normally, this part of the placenta remained healthy. However, male fetuses showing developmental abnormalities also had visible damage to these specialized cells.
paras.zh: 在正常发育的胎儿中，胎盘的这一部分保持健康。然而，表现出发育异常的男性胎儿对这些特化细胞也有明显的损害。

paras.en: Spongiotrophoblasts play an important role in helping the mother's immune system tolerate the developing fetus. This protection is essential because the fetus carries genetic material from both parents and is not genetically identical to the mother.
paras.zh: 海绵滋养层细胞在帮助母亲的免疫系统耐受发育中的胎儿方面发挥着重要作用。这种保护至关重要，因为胎儿携带来自父母双方的遗传物质，并且在遗传上与母亲不同。

paras.en: The researchers found that maternal immune activation could interfere with this protective function. When these placental cells become damaged, the mother's immune response may begin affecting the developing fetus in harmful ways.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，母体免疫激活可能会干扰这种保护功能。当这些胎盘细胞受损时，母亲的免疫反应可能开始以有害的方式影响发育中的胎儿。

paras.en: Why Female Fetuses May Have a Hidden Advantage
paras.zh: 为什么女性胎儿可能具有隐藏的优势

paras.en: The findings raise another intriguing question: Why were male fetuses vulnerable while females appeared unaffected?
paras.zh: 研究结果提出了另一个有趣的问题：为什么男性胎儿容易受到影响，而女性胎儿似乎不受影响？

paras.en: One possibility is that male embryos produce distinctive proteins that can trigger an unfavorable maternal immune response following a viral infection. Another explanation is that female embryos possess some form of protection that helps them withstand inflammation during this sensitive developmental period.
paras.zh: 一种可能性是，雄性胚胎会产生独特的蛋白质，这些蛋白质会在病毒感染后引发不利的母体免疫反应。另一种解释是，雌性胚胎具有某种形式的保护，可以帮助它们在这个敏感的发育时期抵御炎症。

paras.en: Cheadle says, "A protective mechanism may exist within the female that could be harnessed to help the male. We're trying to understand how autism emerges in both sexes," he explains. "The evidence says that there are potentially different mechanisms."
paras.zh: 钱德尔说：“女性体内可能存在一种保护机制，可以用来帮助男性。我们正在试图了解自闭症是如何在两性中出现的，”他解释道。 “证据表明可能存在不同的机制。”

paras.en: These possibilities suggest that biological pathways involved in autism-like development may differ between males and females. Understanding those differences could help researchers identify why some individuals are more vulnerable to certain environmental influences during pregnancy.
paras.zh: 这些可能性表明，男性和女性之间参与自闭症样发育的生物学途径可能不同。了解这些差异可以帮助研究人员确定为什么有些人在怀孕期间更容易受到某些环境影响。

paras.en: Cheadle's team plans to investigate both male and female mice more closely to uncover the mechanisms responsible for these contrasting responses. Their work could eventually identify new targets for treatments and lead to strategies for intervening earlier in developmental processes associated with autism.
paras.zh: 钱德尔的团队计划更仔细地研究雄性和雌性小鼠，以揭示造成这些对比反应的机制。他们的工作最终可能会确定新的治疗目标，并制定早期干预自闭症相关发育过程的策略。

paras.en: Although the findings come from experiments in mice and do not establish that the same mechanisms cause autism in humans, they highlight an unexpected possibility: Important clues to autism's earliest development may lie not only in the brain, but also in the placenta and its interactions with the maternal immune system.
paras.zh: 尽管这些发现来自小鼠实验，并没有证实相同的机制会导致人类自闭症，但它们强调了一种意想不到的可能性：自闭症最早发展的重要线索可能不仅存在于大脑中，还存在于胎盘及其与母体免疫系统的相互作用中。

paras.en: Materials provided by Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由冷泉港实验室提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Irene Sanchez-Martin, Bharti Kukreja, Paige Henderson, Qianyu Lin, Daniel DiMartino, Valerie Bagan, Justin Park, Brian T. Kalish, Lucas Cheadle. Maternal-fetal immune conflict contributes to male-specific impairments in a mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders. Science Advances, 2026; 12 (38) DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aeg0779

articles.title: A 50-year-old mystery of vanishing frogs reveals a hidden killer

paras.en: A 50-year-old mystery of vanishing frogs reveals a hidden killer

- A nearly 50-year-old mystery involving disappearing frogs in Brazil may finally be solved, with scientists uncovering evidence that a deadly fungus swept through the region and devastated vulnerable species. Remarkably, many frog populations have since rebounded, suggesting they developed greater tolerance to the disease that once threatened their survival.

For nearly 50 years, scientists have struggled to explain why frogs began disappearing from Brazil's Atlantic Forest, one of the world's richest regions for amphibian diversity. Beginning in the 1970s, researchers documented dramatic population declines, but the cause of these losses remained uncertain.

Now, scientists have uncovered compelling evidence pointing to a deadly fungal disease as the likely explanation. The findings, published in Molecular Ecology, come from researchers at the Center for Conservation Genomics at the Smithsonian's National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute (NZCBI) and Pennsylvania State University (PSU).

The suspected culprit is chytridiomycosis, often called chytrid, a disease caused by the microscopic fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis. Scientists believe the pathogen originated in Asia before spreading around the world during the 1970s and 1980s. However, the fungus was not formally identified and described until 1999, long after devastating amphibian declines had begun.

By then, hundreds of amphibian species worldwide had been driven toward extinction, and some had already disappeared. Because so many populations collapsed before scientists knew the fungus existed, determining whether it was responsible has been particularly difficult.

"After almost 50 years, we still aren't confident what caused many historical amphibian die-offs, making these declines some of the most enduring cold cases in wildlife epidemiology," said Jack Boyette, an NZCBI graduate fellow and doctoral candidate at PSU who led the research.
A 50-Year-Old Mystery in Brazil's Atlantic Forest
One of these longstanding mysteries centers on the Boracéia Biological Station in Brazil's Atlantic Forest, where amphibian populations experienced severe declines between 1979 and 1982.

Some researchers previously suggested that climate change or unusually extreme weather might have triggered the disappearances. The new findings, however, provide evidence that an emerging fungal disease was spreading through the area at precisely the same time.

"While environmental factors could have played a role, our findings most directly implicate the chytrid fungus, revealing that regional invasion of the pathogen coincided with these unexplained amphibian disappearances," Boyette said.
To investigate what happened, the researchers turned to an unexpected source of evidence: frogs preserved in museum collections decades earlier.

The Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History houses specimens collected by William Ronald Heyer, a former curator of amphibians and reptiles. Heyer conducted five collecting expeditions at Boracéia, including two during the 1970s before the major population declines and three during the 1980s after the die-offs had occurred.

These preserved animals offered scientists a rare opportunity to examine the period before and after the mysterious disappearances. By testing specimens collected at different times, researchers could investigate when the pathogen arrived and how rapidly it spread.
The team analyzed samples from more than 370 preserved amphibians representing 17 species, searching for evidence of chytrid infection and tracking how frequently the fungus appeared over time.
Museum Specimens Reveal a Deadly Fungal Outbreak

The results revealed a striking change. None of the specimens collected before 1979 showed evidence of chytrid infection. Among those collected during the 1980s, however, more than half tested positive for the fungus.
This sharp increase suggests that the pathogen arrived and spread through the local amphibian community around the same time that frog populations were collapsing.
But the researchers also uncovered a surprising pattern.

Species that suffered the most severe declines showed no detectable signs of infection in the preserved specimens. Meanwhile, species whose populations remained relatively stable frequently carried the fungus.

At first glance, these findings might seem to contradict the idea that chytrid caused the disappearances. The researchers believe the explanation may lie in differences in how individual species respond to the disease.

Some frogs may have been naturally capable of tolerating the infection, allowing them to survive even when the fungus was present. More vulnerable species, on the other hand, may have died so quickly after becoming infected that few or no infected individuals were ever collected.

"It's important to keep in mind that not all species suffered catastrophic losses at Boracéia," Boyette said. "The species that didn't decline may have naturally tolerated the fungus, allowing them to become infected without suffering mass mortality. By contrast, the species that declined most dramatically may have been so susceptible that infected frogs died before Heyer could collect them."

Together, the results suggest that chytrid spread rapidly among frogs with little previous exposure to the disease, with potentially devastating consequences for species unable to withstand infection.
Decades-Old Collections Help Solve a Wildlife Cold Case
For Michael Campana, a genomicist at NZCBI who contributed to the research, the findings demonstrate the extraordinary scientific value of natural history museums.

Specimens preserved many decades ago can contain biological evidence that researchers at the time had no way of recognizing. Modern testing methods now make it possible to revisit these collections and investigate outbreaks that occurred long before the responsible pathogens were discovered.

"Museum collectors could not have anticipated how important their collections would be to our modern conservation challenges, but without them, we would never be able to detect pathogens that went unnoticed for decades and reconstruct disease outbreaks that would otherwise remain a mystery," Campana said.
Understanding these past outbreaks could also help scientists anticipate future threats.
One growing concern involves another fungal pathogen, B. salamandrivorans, which is threatening salamander populations in Europe and could pose a serious danger to salamanders in North America.

By reconstructing how earlier fungal diseases emerged, spread, and affected different species, researchers hope to improve their ability to recognize and respond to similar threats before they cause widespread damage.
Brazil's Frogs Show Surprising Signs of Recovery
Despite the devastating losses recorded decades ago, the latest findings also offer encouraging evidence of recovery.
Working with researchers from the University of São Paulo, the team made six visits to Boracéia between 2022 and 2024 to investigate the amphibians living there today.

Of the 17 species represented in Heyer's historical museum collection, researchers located 12 during their modern surveys. The remaining five were not found, leaving their current status uncertain and raising concerns that some may have disappeared from the site entirely.
paras.zh: 在海尔历史博物馆收藏的 17 种物种中，研究人员在现代调查中发现了 12 种。其余五件尚未找到，这使得它们目前的状态不确定，并引发人们担心其中一些可能已经从现场完全消失。

paras.en: Nevertheless, the surveys indicate that most amphibian species at Boracéia have recovered since the severe declines of the early 1980s.

The fungus has not disappeared. Chytrid infections are still present among local frogs, but the pattern of infection suggests that species once heavily affected by the disease may have developed greater tolerance over successive generations.
That increased tolerance could help explain why many populations have survived and rebounded despite continuing exposure to the pathogen.

The findings highlight an important distinction between infection and mortality. A species can carry a dangerous pathogen without necessarily suffering catastrophic losses, particularly if its members can tolerate the infection.
What the Discovery Means for Future Amphibian Survival
paras.zh: 这一发现对未来两栖动物的生存意味着什么

paras.en: Although the evidence strongly implicates chytrid in the historic declines at Boracéia, the researchers caution that their findings apply to this particular location. The results cannot automatically explain amphibian disappearances elsewhere in the Atlantic Forest.

Still, the study provides a compelling explanation for a longstanding local mystery and demonstrates how scientists can use historical specimens to reconstruct outbreaks that would otherwise remain poorly understood.

Researchers are now examining DNA recovered from museum specimens to identify the genetic mechanisms that influenced how amphibians responded to chytrid infections in the past. These analyses could help reveal why some species were devastated while others survived.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正在检查从博物馆标本中回收的 DNA，以确定过去影响两栖动物对壶菌感染反应的遗传机制。这些分析可以帮助揭示为什么一些物种遭到破坏而另一些物种却幸存下来。

paras.en: Separate projects are using ancient environmental DNA to help fill gaps in historical specimen records. This approach involves searching for genetic traces left behind by organisms in their surroundings, potentially providing evidence of species and pathogens that were never directly collected.
paras.zh: 不同的项目正在利用古代环境 DNA 来帮助填补历史标本记录中的空白。这种方法涉及寻找周围环境中生物体留下的遗传痕迹，可能提供从未直接收集的物种和病原体的证据。

paras.en: Together, these efforts could reveal a much clearer history of how chytrid emerged, spread, and affected amphibian biodiversity over the past century.
paras.zh: 总之，这些努力可以更清晰地揭示过去一个世纪壶菌如何出现、传播和影响两栖动物生物多样性的历史。

paras.en: By uncovering the biological changes that helped some frogs survive and recover, scientists may also gain valuable insights into protecting vulnerable species from future fungal epidemics.
paras.zh: 通过揭示帮助一些青蛙生存和恢复的生物变化，科学家们还可能获得宝贵的见解，以保护脆弱物种免受未来真菌流行病的影响。

paras.en: - Jack L. Boyette, Tamilie Carvalho, David Rodriguez, Wesley J. Neely, Daniel Medina, Renato A. Martins, Robert J. Ossiboff, Zaira Gomez, William C. Vuyk, Shannon M. Buttimer, Karen A.
